title: Microsoft 365 admin center: Copilot connectors usage report
summary: The report's controls, default state, licence requirement and rollout targets are supported. Remove the unsupported assurance about indexing, acknowledge the different navigation labels in Microsoft's notice, and keep the recommendation to appoint an owner separate from Microsoft's advice.

claims.quote: "targetDate": "November CY2026"

claims.claim: The roadmap record was modified on 5 November 2026.
Microsoft plans an admin-center report of connector activity, response patterns over time and user-level adoption.
claims.quote: This report provides insights into overall connector activity, and connector powered response patterns over time, along with detailed user-level connectors adoption data.

claims.claim: The report is at Microsoft 365 admin center > Reports > Usage > Microsoft Copilot > Connectors.
claims.quote: In the navigation menu, select Reports. If you don't see Reports, select Show all, and then select Reports. ... Select Usage. ... under Reports, select Microsoft Copilot, and then select Connectors.
claims.fix: Keep the Learn-based path. Add: 'MC1404326 instead labels the path Reporting > Usage > Microsoft 365 Copilot > Connectors.'

claims.claim: No Microsoft Graph call or export route for this Connectors report is documented at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot connectors usage report Microsoft Graph beta API export report settings disable. Opened the report page and copilotReportRoot reference; results describe general Copilot user-detail exports, not a Connectors-report API or export.

claims.claim: The concealment setting is at Settings > Org Settings > Services > Reports > Conceal user, group, and site names in all reports.
claims.quote: Select Org Settings. ... On the Services tab, select Reports. ... In the Reports panel, uncheck the checkbox next to Conceal user, group, and site names in all reports.

claims.claim: PATCH https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/admin/reportSettings with body {"displayConcealedNames": false} shows identifiable report information.
claims.quote: PATCH https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/admin/reportSettings ... displayConcealedNames ... If set to true, all reports conceal user information such as usernames, groups, and sites. If false, all reports show identifiable information.

claims.claim: The report privacy setting is tenant-wide and also affects other usage reports.
claims.quote: By default, all reports hide user information such as usernames, display names, groups, and sites ... This setting also applies to the Microsoft 365 usage reports in Microsoft Graph and Power BI and to the usage reports in Microsoft Teams Admin center.

claims.claim: Global administrators can change the report privacy setting.
claims.quote: Global administrators can update the settings to display concealed information if your organization's privacy practices allow it.

claims.claim: Showing identifiable user information is logged in the Microsoft Purview portal audit log.
claims.quote: Showing identifiable user information is a logged event in the Microsoft Purview portal audit log.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: The report is enabled by default without administrator action.
claims.quote: The report is enabled by default and respects existing permissions. ... No action is required before rollout.

claims.where: front matter: licensing; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The per-user licensing model reflects the notice's requirement for a Microsoft 365 Copilot (Premium) licence to use the feature.
claims.quote: A Microsoft 365 Copilot (Premium) license is required to use this feature

claims.where: What's changing; licensing notes; Risk assessment; Cost and licensing; Scope
claims.claim: Active Connector users counts licensed Microsoft Copilot users who received connector-grounded responses.
claims.quote: Active Connector users shows the total number of users with a Microsoft Copilot license in your organization who received a Copilot-generated response that was grounded on content from Copilot Connectors.

claims.claim: Connector responses counts responses in Copilot Chat, Copilot Search or agents grounded on connector content.
claims.quote: Connector responses shows the total number of responses generated by Copilot Chat, Copilot Search, or in agents that were grounded on content from Copilot Connectors.

claims.claim: Connections used by Copilot counts connections used for grounded responses in Chat and Search.
claims.quote: Connections used by Copilot shows the total number of active Copilot Connector connections that were used when Copilot Chat or Copilot Search generated a response to a user's query that was grounded on content from a Copilot connector.

claims.claim: Connections used by Agents counts connections used for grounded responses by declarative and custom engine agents.
claims.quote: Connections used by Agents shows the total number of active Copilot Connector connections that were used when a declarative agent or custom engine agent generated a response to a user's query that was grounded on content from a Copilot Connector.

claims.claim: The report supports the last 7 or 30 days.
claims.quote: You can view the Microsoft 365 Copilot Connectors report over the last 7 or 30 days.

claims.claim: Report data refreshes within one hour of user activity.
claims.quote: Data that refreshes within one hour of user activity

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment
claims.claim: Active usage requires a connector-grounded cited response, rather than merely opening Chat, Search or an agent.
claims.quote: The user receives a Copilot response that includes grounding (citations) from one or more connectors configured for the organization. ... Simply opening Copilot Chat, Copilot Search, or an agent without submitting a prompt or receiving a connector-grounded response doesn't count as active usage.

claims.claim: Connector usage within Cowork is not yet supported.
claims.quote: Connector usage within Cowork is not yet supported.

claims.claim: The user table covers users licensed for Microsoft Copilot at any point in the past 180 days.
claims.quote: The user-level table in the report shows all users licensed for Microsoft Copilot at any point over the past 180 days, even if the user later removed the license or never had any Copilot active usage.

claims.claim: The user table includes the number of distinct connections used.
claims.quote: Connections used | Total number of distinct connector connections that were used to generate responses grounded on connector content and delivered to users

claims.claim: The user table includes responses received.
claims.quote: Responses Received | The total number of responses delivered to users in Copilot Chat, Copilot Search, or agents that were grounded on content from one or more Copilot connectors.

claims.claim: The user table includes the last activity date.
claims.quote: Last activity date (UTC) | Last date on which the user received a Copilot-generated response that was grounded on content from a Copilot connector.

claims.claim: The connector table identifies connectors by Connection ID rather than by a name.
claims.quote: Connector activity table ... Connection ID | The connector's unique ID ... Active users ... Responses Provided ... Last activity date (UTC)

claims.claim: Usernames, display names, groups and sites are hidden by default in usage reports.
claims.quote: By default, user-specific information like usernames, display names, groups, and sites is hidden in usage reports.

claims.claim: Viewing follows the overview's nine listed administrator and reporting roles.
claims.quote: Global Administrator; Exchange Administrator; SharePoint Administrator; Usage Summary Reports Reader; Reports Reader; Teams Administrator; Teams Communications Administrator; User Experience Success Manager; AI Administrator

claims.claim: Usage Summary Reports Reader and User Experience Success Manager are listed with no user details.
claims.quote: Usage Summary Reports Reader (with no user details). ... User Experience Success Manager (with no user details)

claims.claim: The report's Learn page is marked public preview and warns that functionality may change.
claims.quote: The Copilot Connectors usage report is currently in public preview. Deployment processes and functionality might change before the product becomes generally available.

claims.claim: The report covers Chat, Search and agents at organisation, connector and user level.
claims.quote: track adoption and engagement trends across Copilot Chat, Agents, and Copilot Search ... The report provides insights at the organization, connector, and user level

claims.claim: Measured active usage includes desktop, web and mobile.
claims.quote: Copilot connectors active usage includes intentional user interactions in Copilot Chat, Copilot Search, or agents across desktop, web, and mobile platforms

claims.where: Risk assessment; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The report respects existing permissions.
claims.quote: The report is enabled by default and respects existing permissions.

claims.claim: Microsoft says no action is required before rollout.
claims.quote: No action is required before rollout.

claims.claim: Microsoft says there is no impact to user workflows.
claims.quote: There is no impact to user workflows.

claims.claim: Microsoft suggests informing relevant administrators and analytics stakeholders about the report.
claims.quote: Inform relevant administrators and analytics stakeholders about the new report.

claims.claim: Microsoft suggests reviewing the report after rollout.
claims.quote: Review the report after rollout to assess Copilot connector adoption and usage trends.

claims.claim: Microsoft advises updating internal documentation if it references Copilot reporting.
claims.quote: Update internal documentation if Copilot reporting is referenced.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not clarified whether this report counts both synced and federated connectors or Power Platform and Copilot Studio connectors.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot connectors usage report synced federated Power Platform Copilot Studio connectors counts. Read the report, connector overviews and plugin-capabilities excerpts; none specifies these report inclusion boundaries.

claims.claim: The notice does not specify a separate licence requirement for the administrator viewing the report.
claims.quote: Searched: "Copilot connectors" "usage report" "administrator" "license". Read MC1404326, the report and usage-report overview; the notice gives a feature licence requirement without identifying the viewer's licence.

claims.where: front matter: licensing notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: No separate report price, meter or credit rate is documented as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot connectors usage report licensing administrator license price billing meter premium. Opened report, usage overview, Copilot license options and pay-as-you-go meters; none states a meter, separate price or credit rate for viewing this report.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn documents no setting specific to this report at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: "Copilot connectors" "usage report" "disable"; Copilot connectors usage report Microsoft Graph beta API export report settings disable. Opened report and usage overview; only viewing roles and general report concealment are documented.

claims.claim: The cited copilotReportRoot reference lists user-count and user-detail methods, not a connector report method.
claims.quote: getMicrosoft365CopilotUserCountSummary; getMicrosoft365CopilotUserCountTrend; getMicrosoft365CopilotUsageUserDetail; getMicrosoft365CopilotUsageUserDetailByDate

claims.claim: The report does not change what connectors index.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot connectors usage report changes indexing permissions read only report. Read the report and connector-overview excerpts; neither states whether this report changes indexing. MC1404326 confirms existing permissions, not indexing behaviour.
claims.fix: Replace 'The report does not change what connectors index or who can see it' with 'Microsoft says the report respects existing permissions.'

claims.claim: The Learn report page describes usage counts and no actions taken on connectors, agents or users.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot connectors usage report changes indexing permissions read only report. Read the complete report page, including its metric tables and FAQ; it describes viewing activity, not actions on connectors, agents or users.

claims.claim: The usage overview marks this report N/A for GCC, GCC High and DoD, with release planned in the future.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 Copilot Connectors usage | Yes | N/A^1^ | N/A^1^ | N/A^1^ | N/A^2^ ... N/A^1^: The report will be released in the future.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: The checklist asks readers to review role assignments, but the controls table does not represent that assignment control.
claims.quote: List which administrators hold a role that can view usage reports ... controls: Where administrators view the Copilot connectors usage report; Whether usage reports show user, group and site names
claims.fix: The role-assignment review step has no corresponding control row. Remove that checklist bullet; retain the documented viewer roles in Scope.

claims.claim: The recommendation to name a report owner and inform stakeholders is attributed to Microsoft's notice.
claims.quote: Inform relevant administrators and analytics stakeholders about the new report.
claims.fix: Replace the first Before rollout bullet with 'Name an owner for the Connectors report. Inform relevant administrators and analytics stakeholders about the new report, as Microsoft’s notice suggests.' The owner recommendation is the wiki's advice, not part of the notice.
